s7001_PP_o1: Yes, apple! It is a red or green fruit, and we say "an apple" because apple starts with a vowel sound. Well done. Now say what you like. Write one sentence with "I like ..." and a food word from our list.
s7004_PP_o1: Yes, board! The teacher writes on the board. Well done. Now use our sentence pattern. Look at one thing in your classroom and write: This is a ... Use a word like desk, pen, book or bag.
s7007_PP_o1: Good, you used "There are" and the rest of the sentence is nearly right. But one word needs a change. "Three" means more than one, so the noun needs an ending. Hint: look at the word "window". What do we add for more than one? Try the sentence again.
s7010_PP_o1: Yes, She! Grandmother is a woman, so we use She: "This is my grandmother. She is very kind." Well done. Now your turn. Write two sentences about a person in your family. Start with "This is my ..." and then use He is or She is.
s7013_PP_o1: Correct! We use is with she: "She is at home today." Next one. Write am, is or are: They ___ happy. (answer with only the missing word)
s7016_PP_o1: Yes, are! We use are with they: "They are happy." Well done. Next one. Write am, is or are: My father ___ a pilot. (answer with only the missing word)
s7019_PP_o1: Yes, correct! Three windows is more than one thing, so we say "There are three windows in my room." Well done. Now write your own sentence. Tell me about your room. Use There is or There are and a word from our list.
s7022_PP_o1: Yes, the bedroom is the right place! Your spelling is close, but one letter is missing. Hint: bedroom is two words joined together: bed + room. Try writing it again.
s7025_PP_o1: Yes, "I like rice." is a good sentence. You used I like and a food word, and you wrote a capital letter and a full stop. Well done. Now write one more sentence about a different food. Use I like and a word from our list, for example bread, fish or milk.
s7028_PP_o1: Yes, is! My father is one person, like he, so we use is: "My father is a pilot." Well done. Next one. Write am, is or are: We ___ in the classroom. (answer with only the missing word)
s7031_PP_o1: Good try, but two things need fixing. The word I is always a capital letter, and the sentence needs a full stop at the end. Hint: the sentence begins with I and ends with a full stop. Try again: rewrite "i am ten years old" correctly.
s7034_PP_o1: Yes, had! Have is irregular, so the past form is had, and we do not add -ed. Well done. Next one. Write the past form of 'tell': "Last night he ___ me a story."
s7037_PP_o1: Yes, correct! "The bus is cheap but it is slow." You used but to show a contrast: cheap is good and slow is not good. Well done. Now let's try because, which gives a reason. Join with because: "I am happy. It is my birthday."
s7040_PP_o1: Yes, a! A sandwich is one countable thing, so we say "I'd like a sandwich." Well done. Now try ordering something yourself. Write a polite sentence with "Can I have ..., please?" for a drink at the café.
s7043_PP_o1: Yes, correct! "What did you eat for lunch yesterday?" You used did + the base verb eat, and we do not say "ate" after did. Great. Now ask a different question. Ask a friend where he went last weekend. Start with "Where did you ..."
s7046_PP_o1: Yes, a! A sandwich is one countable thing, so we say "I'd like a sandwich." Well done. Now try ordering something yourself. Write a polite sentence with "Can I have ..., please?" for a drink at the café.
s7049_PP_o1: Yes, told! Tell is irregular, so the past form is told, not "telled". Well done. Next one. Write the past form of 'buy': "Last week she ___ a red hat."
s7052_PP_o1: Let's look at it together. The word is spelled r-e-s-t-a-u-r-a-n-t: restaurant. You wrote it without the letters a and u after "rest". So the sentence is: A chef works in a restaurant. Now try a new one. Complete: "A pilot works at an ___."
s7055_PP_o1: Let's look at it together. The word is spelled a-i-r-p-o-r-t: airport. You wrote "airprt", so the letter o is missing after "p". So the sentence is: A pilot works at an airport. Now try a new one. Complete: "A chef works in a ___."
s7058_PP_o1: Yes, ate! Eat is irregular, so the past form is ate, not "eated". Well done. Now write your own sentence. Tell me one thing you did last weekend. Use went, had or saw.
s7061_PP_o1: Good, you used "has" correctly with he, and you started with a capital letter. But the word order is not right. In English, the adjectives (short, black) go before the noun (hair). Hint: He has ___ ___ hair. Try again, and then add one more sentence about his personality with is.
s7064_PP_o1: Let's look at it together. When it rains, the weather is rainy: rain + y. After "It is" we need the adjective rainy, not the noun rain. So the sentence is: Take an umbrella. It is rainy today. Now try a new one. Complete: "My hat flew away! It is very ___."
s7067_PP_o1: Yes, a little! Rice is uncountable, and only a spoonful means a very small amount, so we say "I have a little rice left." Well done. Now a new one. Write much or many: "Is there ___ milk in the bottle?"
s7070_PP_o1: Yes, visited! Visit is regular, so we add -ed. Well done. Now an irregular verb. Write the past form of 'see': "Last weekend we ___ a film."
